Case study

A sale that was unlikely to close

How we turned one hesitant buyer into three sales

The situation
A client came in to buy in a tower under construction past University Bridge in Mansoura. He was hesitant and leaning toward a small purchase, and as it stood, the sale was unlikely to close.
Understanding him
I did not open with a pitch. I asked about his goals, his budget, how long he planned to hold the property, and what he expected on resale. His real needs pointed somewhere different from what he first asked for.
What we changed
Instead of scattered apartments in different locations, I made the case for a whole floor in one building: simpler to manage and stronger at resale. We then put together the offer that matched what he wanted most.
Closing
We walked him through each concern one by one, until he was comfortable and the decision was his own.
The result
A sale that was not going to happen became three, the entire floor, closed in a single deal.

What I learned

Good selling is not pushing. It is helping the client choose what serves them best.

Case study

Leading three teams at the branch

Keeping three competing teams focused and calm

The situation
As Sales Manager of the New Damietta branch, I ran three sales teams with 20+ salespeople. Competition between the teams was good for results, but it could easily turn into tension that pulled focus away from clients.
Setting the tone
I set clear and fair ground rules, dealt with problems early and directly, and kept every discussion on the numbers rather than on personalities. The aim was a calm floor where competing felt motivating, not stressful.
Developing the people
I shared my field experience at every level: team leaders on coaching and managing their teams, fresh salespeople on the sales cycle and handling clients, and juniors with step-by-step guidance.
How I taught
I taught by doing: sitting in on client meetings, supporting negotiations, and reviewing closed and lost deals together afterward, so everyone learned from real cases.
The result
Three teams that competed without friction, team leaders able to run their own teams, and new salespeople who grew into the role, with the branch reaching EGP 40M in sales.

What I learned

A manager's job is not only hitting the number. It is building people who can hit it without you.
